CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. Gomez returns for routine follow-up of psoriatic arthritis. She reports her condition is well-controlled on her current regimen. She has been successfully tapering prednisone and is currently on 1 mg daily. She occasionally takes an additional dose approximately once per week when experiencing increased foot pain, particularly on days with increased physical activity. Methotrexate has been very effective for management of her joint pain. She previously discontinued methotrexate for one week prior to receiving her first COVID-19 vaccine due to concerns about potential interference with vaccine efficacy based on informational materials received. This resulted in significant pain exacerbation. She was advised to continue methotrexate with her second vaccine dose. She also reports easy bruising on her extremities that she does not feel when it occurs. This has been attributed to prednisone use.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Joint pain improved with methotrexate. Foot pain worse with increased activity. Easy bruising of extremities noted. Nail ridges present on toes. No other acute complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily (to be discontinued)
Methotrexate (continuing)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works a desk job. Experiences increased foot pain with increased physical activity on days off.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Feet and lower extremities examined with shoes and socks removed. Mild joint tenderness noted in foot joints and other joints. Knee flexion and extension with good range of motion, improved compared to prior to methotrexate dose increase. Toe flexion intact with good range of motion. Nail ridges present bilaterally, consistent with psoriasis.

RESULTS
No acute laboratory findings. Blood work to be scheduled.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis, stable on current regimen with good response to methotrexate.
1. Discontinue prednisone effective today; monitor for symptom changes and reassess bruising
2. Continue methotrexate; monitor closely given high-risk medication profile
3. Schedule blood work appointment at front desk prior to departure
4. Follow-up visit in 3 months
